title: Sleep-Talking Sabotage
logline: At 3am Poppy says the wrong name out loud, Élodie hears it and rates it a six, and by sunset the whole villa is being scored out of ten by people who cannot admit what they want.

scenes.visual: Dark bedroom, moonlight stripes. Poppy in Union Jack pyjama crop top asleep mouth-open mid-murmur; Matteo beside her in white linen shirt smiling blissfully in his sleep; Élodie two beds over, sleek dark bob on the pillow, eyes wide open, red lip, utterly unimpressed.

lines.speaker: elodie-france
lines.delivery: deadpan whisper into the dark, eyes never blinking

scenes.visual: Poolside. Lucas in open canary-yellow Brazil jersey mid-hug with Élodie, who accepts it like paperwork; Poppy just behind, arms folded, smile clamped tight; Matteo in tricolore apron watching from a sun-lounger with tragic eyebrows; Sienna dripping wet, zinc stripe, grinning at all of it.

lines.speaker: matteo-italy
lines.delivery: quiet operatic doom, like declaring war

scenes.visual: Firepit at dusk. Sienna in green-and-gold surf top leaning forward like a bookmaker; Élodie serene in her tricolore scarf holding up five fingers; Lucas's grin cracking; Poppy half-standing, furious; Matteo slamming a steaming lasagne onto the table; Brock beaming in his star-print shorts.

lines.speaker: sienna-australia
lines.text: Rate the men. Out of ten. Go.

lines.speaker: lucas-brazil
lines.text: Five is a nice number, no?

lines.speaker: poppy-uk
lines.text: A five? He's the best thing here.
lines.delivery: too loud, too fast, immediately regretting it

scenes.visual: Firelight close on three faces: Poppy mid-accusation, mouth open; Élodie calm, chin lifted, delivering the line like a receipt; Lucas between them, beaded necklace catching light, brow slowly folding into confusion.

lines.speaker: poppy-uk
lines.text: You rate him a five and you—

lines.speaker: elodie-france
lines.text: Day two. I kissed him. Two minutes.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: It was the balcony she pretended not to see.

lines.speaker: lucas-brazil
lines.text: That was a kiss? I filed it as a hug.

scenes.visual: Spill Room. Élodie alone in tiny sunglasses and tricolore scarf, arms crossed, one eyebrow up, denying everything with her mouth and confessing with her entire face.

lines.speaker: elodie-france
lines.text: Do I want Lucas? C'est un non.
lines.delivery: icy denial, hard cut, then a betrayed whisper on the last three words

scenes.visual: Sunset walkway, gate swinging open. Alejandro in crimson shirt with gold trim and red sash, one red carnation, full smolder. Greta in black-red-gold kit blocking him with a clipboard; Rohan in his saffron-white-green polo frantically flipping notebook pages.

lines.speaker: greta-germany
lines.text: You are not on the schedule.

scenes.visual: Terrace at last light. Alejandro alone, crimson shirt and gold sash, twirling the carnation, looking straight down the lens with a smolder that took eleven months of mirror practice.

lines.speaker: alejandro-spain
lines.text: She gives numbers. Tomorrow I give her one.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: What number does he give Élodie?

caption: She rated him a FIVE with a nine on her whole face 💀 and Poppy talked in her sleep at 3am. Guess Alejandro's number before Ep 2 👇
musicDirection: Original royalty-free tracks only. 3am hook: sparse music-box plink with a heartbeat pulse. Kitchen: bright plucked ukulele-marimba gossip bed. Poolside: sunny bossa-flavoured shaker groove. Firepit dare: tick-tock percussion building under each rating, hard brass sting on the lasagne gavel. Twist: everything drops to a single sustained cello note and room tone. Arrival: one flamenco-adjacent guitar flourish, generated, no lyrics. Endcard: single cheeky pizzicato button.
continuityNotes: Élodie's out-of-ten rating system is the season's comic currency; established Ep1 as a callback engine (six, five, four).
Poppy sleep-said 'Lucas' at 3am; Élodie heard it and rated it a six. Poppy knows she talked and is terrified.
Élodie kissed Lucas on day two for two minutes; Lucas 'filed it as a hug' and still doesn't grasp it. Poppy half-saw it from the balcony.
Brock believes 'thank you for the water' is a commitment; Élodie has scored the water a four. He will escalate.
Matteo built a lasagne for eleven as a loyalty alarm — carbohydrates are his conflict language going forward.
Lucas will not go past the pool steps. Nobody has asked why yet.
Poppy's poetry notebook under the mattress is still unrevealed on camera.
Alejandro arrived unscheduled with one red carnation, off Greta's clipboard and outside Rohan's framework, and is already scoring Élodie sight unseen.
